correctness.rationale: For arbitrary nonempty factor sets and possibly improper/nonprincipal filters, product membership of the union of two coordinate cylinders is equivalent to membership of at least one cylinder base in its factor filter. Iteration from the empty truth set proves the identity for every n. In the finite witness S is the transitive strict chain plus a loop, R adds a root-to-loop arrow and stays transitive; S composed with S is contained in R, so mix holds. All earlier depths have identical truth values, but depth n fails at the root. The reproduced standalone bit-set checker tested 8,784 filter pairs through depth 7 and 16 independence frames; these tests are corroborative, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The first unresolved nonserial full neighborhood products in the 2026 source require interactions beyond the fusion-plus-mix axioms that suffice for serial cases. The all-depth exact failure-set identity is a structural lemma valid for arbitrary neighborhood filters; its finite transitive separating frames show that adding any finite initial selection of these natural necessary conditions is insufficient. This identifies a genuine unbounded obstruction rather than arbitrary finite parameter census, while carefully not claiming full nonfinite axiomatizability.
